GEOGRAPHY: McDonald's reports revenue by its three segments; International Operated Markets covers markets such as Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain and the U.K., and the third segment combines developmental-licensee markets (including China and Japan) with corporate activities. footprint.notes: Restaurant counts by market come from McDonald's 'Restaurants by Market 2025' PDF (investor relations; year-end 2025, 45,356 restaurants); 97 markets covering 114 countries. Several markets consolidate other countries: United States includes Cuba, Guam and Saipan; Australia includes American Samoa, Fiji, New Caledonia, Tahiti and Western Samoa; France includes Monaco; Spain includes Andorra and Gibraltar; Switzerland includes Liechtenstein; United Kingdom includes the Isle of Man, Jersey, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. 'St. Marten' and 'Virgin Islands' are kept as unnamed-country regions because the document does not say which territory (Dutch Sint Maarten vs. French Saint-Martin; U.S. vs. British Virgin Islands) is meant. Sri Lanka, which showed 0 restaurants at year-end 2024, is no longer listed in the 2025 edition, so its row was removed. No restaurant count by U.S. state was found in the FY2025 10-K or in the restaurant-count document, so usStates is null. The FY2025 10-K says company employees totaled over 150,000 at year-end 2025, about 70% outside the U.S.; no country split was derived. Segment subtotals (IOM 10,845; IDL 20,805) were not repeated as regions.

source.quote: Our median employee for 2025 is a restaurant crew employee located in Poland and in 2025 had total compensation of $19,020 as calculated in accordance with the Summary Compensation Table rules.

pay.notes: Employees: the 10-K gives a floor ('over 150,000'), recorded as 150,000; it excludes the over two million people who work in franchised restaurants. Payroll: the income statement's 'Payroll & employee benefits' (2,905 million) covers only Company-owned and operated restaurants (support-staff payroll sits in SG&A), so it is not a total staff cost and the proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used: a part-time-inclusive restaurant crew employee in Poland, identified by annualizing one month's wages for employees on October 1, 2025 (CEO pay ratio 1,082:1).
